rationale: A wins because it respects the most dangerous fact in the brief: Mercury is not a bank. Its angle "Mercury wants to hold consumers' money without being a bank" is sharp, grounded, and useful; B keeps stepping on the rake with "the bank startups fled to after SVB" and "now a consumer bank." B has good bones, but calling the non-bank a bank is not a cosmetic error in a banking story.
gaps_in_A: "Consumer banking will test that claim" slightly overstates what the launch proves; consumer expansion tests future economics more than the existing profitability claim.
"The launch is live today" assumes the announcement timing from the update; acceptable, but it should stay tied to the 2026-06-09 launch peg, not become generic launch boilerplate.
The economics angle needs one harder line on what happens if Mercury cannot substantiate profitability: hold it, do not pitch it as scrutiny bait.
gaps_in_B: "the bank startups fled to after SVB" is sloppy and overclaimed. The update says Mercury became known as a startup-banking alternative after SVB, not that startups fled to it.
"business-only bank" and "now a consumer bank" contradict the supplied fact that Mercury uses partner banks and does not have a bank charter. That is the fact you cannot fumble.
"What the SVB windfall became" invents a financial windfall. The brief gives reputation, 200,000 businesses, and a profit claim; it does not give post-SVB deposit gain or revenue.

"whether the obvious wedge is the founders and employees who already bank at those 200,000 companies" is a plausible question, but still speculative. It needs to be framed as unproven until Mercury confirms invite priority.
